findings.claim: The blueprint maps checking-ai-changes objective o3, which requires the learner to decide and cite specific evidence, to a single MCQ. Selecting a supplied option can check recognition of a justified decision, but it does not directly elicit the learner's own evidence citation, so the format does not fully match the observable performance that the blueprint claims to cover.
findings.recommendation: Keep the fixed syllabus and item counts. Replace this blueprint reference with checking-ai-changes#o1, whose claim-to-diff-line matching is directly elicitable by a scenario-based MCQ, or use an assessment format that requires the learner to supply the evidence citation before claiming coverage of o3.

findings.claim: The intake still directs readers to intake-reconciliation.json.txt even though the final evidence file was renamed to intake-reconciliation.json. This stale path makes the stated basis for the accepted objective and title changes harder to locate.
findings.recommendation: Change the cross-reference to evidence/git-linux-ai-foundations/intake-reconciliation.json (or the correct relative filename) so the applicability and objective decisions point to the evidence file that exists in the final tree.

items.note: Resolved on the final bytes at 5f744e623022f550964dc5ecbd57c26b71c14743: the blueprint now declares 16 representative objectives rather than all 49, uses exact topic objective ids, maps all 10 MCQ objectives and six coding objectives through objectiveFormats, and plausibly combines the six hands-on objectives into three short tasks. The narrower format mismatch for checking-ai-changes#o3 is recorded separately as new medium finding education2-01; it does not reopen the earlier high finding about implausible whole-course coverage.
